clue.text: Cereal for all to see, firm and good — a plentiful supply

parts.note: corn is a cereal crop
U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for everyone
CO is short for company, a firm
PI, short for pious, is crosswordese for good

explanation.surface: An advert boasting of a grain company's wholesome, abundant produce.
explanation.definitionFit: The horn of plenty symbolises abundance, so the word is used for any overflowing stock of things.

clue.text: Device used in filming river over time

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the second

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A film crew's gear set up beside a river over a long shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: A film shoot records its pictures with this machine.

clue.text: Predicted sequence of events in race so inaccurately

indicators.note: written inaccurately, the letters of these words land in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A forecast of how a race will go that turns out to be wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A planner's outline of how things are expected to unfold is a projected course of events.

clue.text: Top vicar read up on Bible passage endlessly

indicators.note: in a down clue, read up means the letters are taken from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is the title of a vicar

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a text is a short passage of scripture quoted for a sermon

explanation.surface: A senior clergyman studies a passage of scripture in his pulpit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like an adjective for the vicar but is the definition. REV read up gives VER; TEXT without its end gives TEX.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest point of a shape or a hill is its apex, its summit.

clue.text: Party member in protest about renegade

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
C is short for circa, Latin for about
a rat is someone who deserts their side

explanation.surface: A politician caught up in a demonstration against a turncoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of one of the two main US political parties, a party member in the American system.

clue.text: Object of admiration I study

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: Someone admiring whatever they happen to be studying.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrated figure that people revere is an idol, a person looked up to.

clue.text: Mock exam's third and final part

parts.note: cod means mock or sham, as in cod Latin

indicators.note: third points to the third letter of the word that precedes it here

explanation.surface: A student describing the last section of a practice exam paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mock exam' reads as a practice test, but 'Mock' alone gives COD, a British word for fake.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, the closing passage that rounds off a movement is its concluding section.

clue.text: Skill in force mostly supplied by number connected with church

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter of the word is kept

parts.note: to compel is to force
ten is a number
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Ability at a job reinforced by a figure linked to a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Being able to do a task properly is ability, a synonym of skill.

clue.text: Boy, small, breaking main rule badly

indicators.note: the boy and small pieces break into the middle of the word for main, splitting it in two

parts.note: master as an adjective means main, as in master bedroom
a lad is a boy
mini means small

explanation.surface: A small boy disrupting the main rule of a household by behaving badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main rule' looks like one phrase, but the definition starts at 'rule'; 'main' is master in its adjective sense, and 'breaking' splits it open around the boy and the small one.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage or govern incompetently or dishonestly is to misgovern, ruling poorly.

clue.text: Understand a line including name of Hades?

indicators.note: the letters for understand, a and line together take the abbreviation for name inside them

parts.note: to infer is to understand or deduce

explanation.surface: A puzzled reader trying to find the name of Hades within a line of text.
explanation.definitionFit: Hades is the underworld, so something belonging to it is hellish, from the Latin for lower regions.

clue.text: Difficult time facing sailors in boat

indicators.note: the sailors are placed in the boat, inside its letters

parts.note: a hoy is a small coastal sailing vessel
RN is the Royal Navy, the sailors

explanation.surface: A tough spell for crew members aboard a little vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A problem full of prickles, like a bramble, is a tricky or awkward one.

clue.text: Head for lunch in part of London and look for cake

parts.note: EC is the East Central postcode district of London, the City

indicators.note: head for here means the first letter of the following word

parts.note: an air is a look or appearance, as in an air of mystery

explanation.surface: Someone heading to the City at lunchtime in search of a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is a London postal district covering the City, the financial centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream-filled choux pastry finger topped with chocolate is a kind of small cake.

clue.text: Amount of medicine containing a lot of added sugar

indicators.note: the dose holds the other piece inside its letters

parts.note: a dose is a measured amount of medicine

indicators.note: a lot of means most of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: extra means added, additional

explanation.surface: A dose of medicine laced with plenty of extra sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'added sugar' reads as one phrase on the surface; 'sugar' alone is the definition, and 'a lot of' keeps all of the word for added but its final A.
explanation.definitionFit: Glucose found in nature is also called by this name, a simple sugar.

clue.text: Letters going up in smoke?

parts.note: not burning post but words traced in the sky in an aircraft's vapour trail

explanation.definitionFit: Pilots form words in the sky with smoke trails, so the letters literally rise up in smoke.

clue.text: Plan with modernity put into action, for the most part

indicators.note: the letters are set to work in a new order, rearranged

explanation.surface: A strategy for modernisation is implemented, at least mostly.
explanation.definitionFit: Mainly, chiefly, or for the greater part all mean the same thing.

clue.text: Look in outlet for portion of meat

indicators.note: the word for look goes inside the word for outlet

parts.note: an escape is an outlet, as for gas or steam
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Spotting a cut of meat on sale in a shop outlet.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin slice of boneless meat, often veal, beaten flat and fried, is a cut of meat.

clue.text: The foolish may scorn Nicam and the like

indicators.note: foolish describes the letters as behaving in a silly way, so they are scrambled

explanation.surface: Only a fool would sneer at an audio standard like Nicam.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicam, the TV stereo sound system, stands for near-instantaneous companded audio multiplex, so it is formed from initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Words formed from the initials of a phrase, as Nicam is, are examples of this kind of abbreviation.

clue.text: Academic examination, one entered by good composer

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is an academic

indicators.note: the scan and one together are entered by the letter for good, which goes inside

parts.note: a scan is a medical examination
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A scholar sits an exam and a good candidate gets through.
explanation.walkthrough: G goes between SCA and NI.
explanation.definitionFit: Pietro Mascagni was the Italian who wrote the opera Cavalleria Rusticana.

clue.text: Monster with no drink getting upset

indicators.note: in a down clue an upset turns the letters upside down, so they read backwards

parts.note: grog is a drink, originally rum and water

explanation.surface: A monstrous person turns nasty when denied a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Medusa and her sisters were snake-haired creatures of Greek myth, whose gaze turned people to stone.

clue.text: Prize for which revolutionary keeps fighting

indicators.note: the word for revolutionary keeps the other piece held inside it

parts.note: a red is a revolutionary communist
war is fighting

explanation.surface: A rebel keeps on fighting to win a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: Something given in return for an achievement is a prize or bounty.

clue.text: Group of protesters lacking power after opening of wide gate

indicators.note: the shortened picket comes after the opening letter of wide
opening of means the first letter of the following word
lacking means the letter for power is taken away

parts.note: a picket is a group of strikers protesting outside a workplace

explanation.surface: Protesters standing at a wide gate without enough strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gate' looks like scenery for the picket line, but it is the definition; a wicket is an old word for a small gate, not only the cricket stumps. 'lacking' drops the P.
explanation.definitionFit: A wicket is a small gate or door, often set within a larger one.

clue.text: Man, one working as a lumberjack?

definitions.meaning: a colloquial form of fellow, a chap
someone who fells trees for a living

explanation.definitionFit: Fellow is informally spelt this way for a man, and a tree-cutter literally fells timber.

clue.text: Make sound of eagle

indicators.note: sound of tells us the bird's name is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: an erne is a sea eagle

explanation.surface: Imitating the cry of an eagle.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn money is to make it, as in make a living.

clue.text: A session of cricket practice set about by Cork, say, showing persistence

indicators.note: set about means turned around, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: a net is a cricket practice session in a netted lane
Cork is an Irish city

explanation.surface: Batting practice in Cork shows how determined the players are.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, nets are practice sessions where batters face bowlers inside netting. 'set about' turns A NET into TENA.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggedness, refusing to let go, is perseverance.

clue.text: Exclamation by prime minister, grasping jargon sent over in coded message

parts.note: a cry is an exclamation

indicators.note: the PM holds the other piece inside its letters
sent over means turned over, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: argot is jargon, specialist slang

explanation.surface: A prime minister shouts while clutching a jargon-filled secret dispatch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent over' turns the jargon word backwards, giving TOGRA, which the prime minister's two letters grasp.
explanation.definitionFit: A text written in cipher, needing to be decoded, is a coded message.

clue.text: Long periods in part of prince on stage

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An actor playing a prince spends ages on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Ages and aeons are both vast stretches of time.
